extracted.intended_audience: legal researchers, historians, lawyers, and members of the public consulting historical U.S. statutes
extracted.subtask_description: Transcription of 1791 statutory provisions relating to the incorporation and regulation of the Bank of the United States, including penalties, lending limits, receivability of bank notes, subscription authority, and subscription procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture for persons ordering unlawful dealing or trading
rubrics_metrics.description: All and every person and persons, by whom any order or direction for so dealing or trading shall have been given, and all and every person and persons who shall have been concerned as parties or agents therein, shall forfeit and lose treble the value of the goods, wares, merchandises, and commodities, in which such dealing and trade shall have been; one half thereof to the use of the informer, and the other half thereof to the use of the United States, to be recovered with costs of suit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty is treble the value of the goods involved; recovery includes costs of suit; proceeds split half to informer and half to United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition and penalty for unlawful advances or loans by the corporation (Sec. 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the said corporation shall advance or lend any sum, for the use or on account of the government of the United States, to an amount exceeding one hundred thousand dollars; or of any particular state to an amount exceeding fifty thousand dollars; or of any foreign prince or state, (unless previously authorized thereto by a law of the United States,) all and every person and persons, by and with whose order, agreement, consent, approbation, or connivance, such unlawful advance or loan shall have been made, upon conviction thereof, shall forfeit and pay, for every such offence, treble the value or amount of the sum or sums which shall have been so unlawfully advanced or lent; one fifth thereof to the use of the informer, and the residue thereof to the use of the United States; to be disposed of by law and not otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets numeric lending limits (US: $100,000; any one state: $50,000; foreign prince/state: only if previously authorized); violation triggers treble forfeiture, with one-fifth to informer and remainder to the United States; requires conviction; disposition subject to law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receivability of bank bills or notes in payments to the United States (Sec. 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: That the bills or notes of the said corporation, originally made payable, or which shall have become payable on demand, in gold and silver coin, shall be receivable in all payments to the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bank notes that are payable (or have become payable) on demand in gold and silver coin are declared acceptable for any payment due to the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential authority to subscribe to bank stock on behalf of the United States (Sec. 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall be lawful for the President of the United States, at any time or times, within eighteen months after the first day of April next, to cause a subscription to be made to the stock of the said corporation, as part of the aforesaid capital stock of ten millions of dollars, on behalf of the United States, to an amount not exceeding two millions of dollars; to be paid out of the monies which shall be borrowed by virtue of either of the acts ... borrowing of the bank an equal sum, to be applied to the purposes, for which the said monies shall have been procured; reimbursable in ten years, by equal annual instalments; or at any time sooner, or in any greater proportions, that the government may think fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizes President to subscribe up to $2,000,000 of the bank's capital as part of $10,000,000 total; payment source specified (borrowed monies under cited acts); requires the bank to borrow an equal sum; repayment schedule: reimbursable in ten years by equal annual installments, subject to earlier or larger repayment as government decides; time limit for subscription is within 18 months after specified date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on establishing other banks during corporation's continuance (Sec. 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: That no other bank shall be established by any future law of the United States, during the continuance of the corporation hereby created; for which the faith of the United States is hereby pledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express ban on creating competing banks by future legislation while this corporation exists; includes a pledge of the faith of the United States to that effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postponement of opening subscriptions to bank stock (Chap. XI, Sec. 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: That the subscriptions to the stock of the bank of the United States, as provided by the act, intituled 'An act to incorporate the subscribers to the bank of the United States,' shall not be opened until the first Monday in July next.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative timing rule delaying the opening of stock subscriptions until a specified date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of portion of first payment in six percent certificates (Chap. XI, Sec. 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: That so much of the first payment as by the said act is directed to be in the six per cent. certificates of the United States, may be deferred until the first Monday in January next.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits deferral of the portion of the initial payment that is to be made in specified government certificates until a named future date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on number of shares to be subscribed at one time (Chap. XI, Sec. 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: That no person, corporation, or body politic, except in behalf of the United States, shall, for the space ... Not more than thirty shares to be subscribed at one time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes a numeric cap (not more than thirty shares) on subscription by any single person/corporation/body politic at one time; text indicates exception for subscriptions on behalf of the United States. (Note: scanned text is partially truncated but core rule limiting subscriptions to thirty shares is explicit.)
